title: Bekamak Semi-Automatic Band Saws (BMSY) | NovoTech Canada
meta_description: Bekamak BMSY semi-automatic band saws in Canada: hydraulic vise, automatic bow return, single- and double-miter heads to 60°, Ø9″ to Ø17-3/8″ (230–440 mm). Specs in inches and mm, support in Mississauga.
intro: The workhorse of most fabrication shops: the operator loads the bar and presses start; the hydraulic vise clamps, the bow cuts at the set feed rate and lifts clear when the cut is done. Bekamak's BMSY pivot saws come with single- or double-miter heads for structural steel, inverter blade speed and hydro-mechanical blade tension — from Ø9″ to Ø17-3/8″ (230–440 mm).

faq_title: Questions we get asked about Bekamak semi-automatic band saws

faq.q: What is the difference between a semi-automatic and a fully automatic band saw?
faq.a: A semi-automatic saw makes one cut per start: it clamps, cuts and lifts the bow, then waits for the operator to feed the next piece. A fully automatic saw also feeds the material to length (by rollers or a shuttle vise) and repeats the cycle for the programmed quantity. See the Bekamak automatic band saws page.

A single-miter head (BMSY 320G/GL) swivels to one side, so angled parts are cut by flipping the bar. A double-miter head (BMSY DG/DGH) swivels both ways — +60° right, −45° left — which saves handling on frames and trusses with opposite angles.

faq.q: What does the DGH suffix mean?
faq.a: DGH models position the saw head hydraulically for miter angles instead of by hand, and include hydraulic head lifting — useful on the larger 320–440 mm machines where the bow is heavy.
Yes, with the optional hydraulic top clamping, which presses a bundle of tubes or bars down while the side vise holds it. Ask us about bundle sizes for the model you need.
